what: Connects uninsured DuPage residents to care through partner providers.
Recipient-budget scenario models Access DuPage morbidity; over $50m reported partner care is outside its central numerator.
Central illustrative cost: $4,359,839 per 10 Chicago-MSA QALYs (9.535788 annual modeled QALYs).
strengths: Original audit identifies enrollees and costs.
The documented donated-provider network is a plausible care-access channel.
reservations: Central price excludes substantial provider resources and is not comparable to a full-resource estimate.
Geographic and counterfactual care shares are unmeasured.

sections.what: DHC operates Access DuPage, Silver Access, pharmacy, education and debt navigation. Access requires DuPage residence and ineligibility for other insurance. Some copayments remain. Official financial page identifies EIN 36-4448208; canonical slug retained.
sections.monitoring: Audit note 8 reports 5,871 enrollees. Assume 75% treated and 25% of treated obtain additional meaningful relief: neither measured. Request completed treatment, clinical response, utility and alternative care. Oregon randomized insurance evidence found depression benefit without significant physical-health gains in two years; not a recipient-specific calibration.
sections.qualitative: Coordination may unlock specialty care; clinician availability and existing charity care constrain expansion. Other programs retain full costs but no separate health credit because benefits and overlap are unknown, not a lower bound. Debt dollars are not QALYs.
sections.cost: FY2025 full expense $4,157,450 includes support and $207,956 pantry in-kind. Formula: 5,871 × 0.75 treated × 0.25 additional responders × 0.05 utility × 0.5 year × 0.35 financing additionality × 0.99 MSA. Note 8 reports over $50 million partner donated services outside recipient accounts. Adding $50 million tests reported-value resource scope; it is not opportunity cost and may overlap. The $50 million add-on is a rounded floor of reported value, not the actual total. It cannot establish economic opportunity cost or a comparable all-resource rank.
sections.funding: Operating revenue $4,522,036, nonoperating income $181,919, net assets $5,574,279. Building purchase $1,138,000 used reserves and was capitalized; recurring cost retains depreciation instead of adding purchase again. No priced unfunded expansion found; financing factor is judgment.

model.costScope: Full DHC recipient expense, including recorded pantry in-kind; excludes partner care reported above $50m. This is a recipient-budget perspective, not full economic resource cost. The $50m sensitivity is a rounded reported-value floor illustration, not an upper bound or measured opportunity cost.
model.counterfactual: a removes equivalent care elsewhere and ineffective care; b separately removes replacement financing/volunteer capacity. One morbidity pathway avoids double counting.
model.geographicAttribution: DuPage residence required; .99 allows mobility/errors within the pinned MSA framework.
model.uncertainty: Central illustrative scenario and favorable/poor bounds are judgments, not calibrated EV or confidence interval. Cross-recipient results cannot be summed without deduplication. These costs are whole-portfolio equivalents, not marginal gift purchase guarantees. Cost numerators use different accounting recognition of donated care; central prices must not be interpreted as a comparable economic-efficiency ranking. Favorable and poor scenarios are illustrative cases, not exhaustive bounds.
